To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the joint spatial statistical model of RFI in a multiantenna wireless system is a mixture of the Middleton Class A and symmetric alpha stable distributions.

the joint spatial statistical model of multiantenna RFI generated from randomly distributed interfering sources can be derived using statistical-physical interference propagation mechanisms, that the joint spatial model captures a continuum from spatially independent to spatially isotropic RFI, and that our proposed model can be applied to various wireless network environments.

we derived a joint spatial statistical model for RFI generated from multiple uncoordinated interfering devices in wireless networks, and that the model is applicable to many wireless network environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical characterization of interference in a multiantenna environment, and the development of a joint spatial statistical model for RFI generated from interfering sources.
the development and analysis of statistical models for interference generated by uncoordinated sources in wireless networks.
the derivation of joint statistics for RFI in multiantenna receivers, which are useful for modeling and analysis in wireless communications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed joint spatial statistical RFI model is the first statistical model of RFI for multiantenna receivers that is both spatially dependent and statistically-physically motivated.
the proposed statistical model is the only one in the literature that captures a continuum of spatial statistics between spatially independent (Rayleigh fading) and spatially isotropc (Rice fading).

we have derived joint statistical models for multiantenna RFI, based on statistical- physical interference generation and propagation, which capture a continuum between spatial independence and isotropy, and hence include many previous results as limiting cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed model is more general than previous models, and can be used to predict the performance of wireless systems operating in various network environments.

our proposed joint spatial statistical models provide a statistical-physically derived and analytically tractable framework to capture the statistical properties of RFI in wireless networks with multiantenna receivers.
we provide a unified framework for modeling joint spatial statistics of RFI for multiantenna receivers in various network environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial statistics of multiantennas RFI are highly dependent on the network environment.
joint spatial statistical models are necessary to capture the spatial structure of RFI generated by uncoordinated interfering devices.
the spatial statistics of interference in a multiantenna system is not only dependent on the number of antennas, but also on the distribution of the interference sources around the antenna array.
